raw_text:
Here’s a complete, integrated 12‑week plan — strength, cardio, nutrition, recovery/mobility — summarized week‑by‑week and ready to use with your client. It respects the constraints: no jumping, avoid deep knee flexion under load (keep loaded knee flexion to ~60° or pain‑free range), protect the repaired medial meniscus, and progress to a strong, ski‑ready Week 12. The program uses a 5‑day weekly template (3 strength sessions + 2 higher‑intensity low‑impact cardio sessions), with progressive blocks and peak/tapering. I’ve included key coaching cues, progression rules, and monitoring checkpoints.

Quick facts
- Client: 36, recreational lifter, right medial meniscus repair 6 months ago — surgeon cleared for low‑impact strength only.
- Goal: strength and return to skiing, maintain weight.
- Weekly structure (typical): Mon Strength A (Lower), Tue Cardio A (HIIT/mixed modal), Wed Strength B (Upper), Thu Cardio B (Ski power/threshold), Fri Strength C (Lower unilateral & transfer), Sat active recovery or pool, Sun rest.
- Strength sessions: controlled tempo, hip‑dominant emphasis, box/belt/trap‑bar alternatives to reduce compressive deep squat stress. Avoid deep loaded knee flexion; use partial/box squats (~60°), belt squats, trap‑bar, hip thrusts, RDLs, single‑leg RDLs with limited knee bend.
- Cardio: low‑impact only (bike, assault bike, ski‑erg, skier simulator, slideboard, sled pushes, pool). Two sessions/week; progressively challenging, mixed modalities, power intervals and tempo work.
- Nutrition: maintain weight (maintenance calories), protein 1.6–2.0 g/kg/day, carbs timed around training; slight carb bump on high volume weeks. Creatine and omega‑3 optional.
- Recovery/mobility: daily micro‑routine, pre/post workout protocols, 2–3 extended mobility sessions/week, foam rolling, targeted quad/glute activation, ankle & thoracic mobility. Monitor swelling and pain; consult physio if needed.

Phases overview
- Phase 1 Weeks 1–3: Rehab consolidation — control, quad activation within safe ROM, hip strength, neuromuscular control. Moderate volume.
- Ramp Week 4 → Intensified Block Weeks 5–8: Aggressive progressive overload — higher volume and cardio volume, added optional finishers. Monitor knee closely.
- Peak Block Weeks 9–12: Convert to neural strength and ski transfer; heavy low‑rep lifts, reduced accessory volume, taper Week 12 to feel powerful and fresh.

Progression rules (apply throughout)
- Increase sets/volume before heavy load increases. When adding load keep form flawless and no sharp knee pain.
- Small load increases: 2.5–5% per week when pain‑free and technique stable.
- For cardio: increase intervals/duration then reduce rest; track watts/calories or RPE. If knee irritation, swap to pool/upper‑body ergometer and reduce volume.
- Deload weeks: Week 4 was a planned ramp; Week 8 is consolidation; Week 12 is taper. Use symptom logs to autoregulate.

Sample exercise selection (examples you’ll use each session)
- Lower (A): Box/safety‑bar squat to ~60°; trap‑bar deadlift; RDLs; leg press partial; hip thrusts; short‑arc extensions.
- Unilateral (C): Single‑leg RDLs (limited knee bend); Bulgarian split‑squat (shallow); single‑leg press (partial); cable chops for ski transfer.
- Upper (B): Bench/incline press; weighted pull‑ups/rows; overhead press; carries; core anti‑rotation.
- Cardio A (Tue): Mixed‑modal HIIT — pyramids on bike + ski‑erg/battle rope/sled rounds.
- Cardio B (Thu): Ski‑erg power intervals + tempo block on bike/erg.

Week‑by‑week summary

Weeks 1–3 (Phase 1 — Rehab consolidation)
- Strength (3x/week): Emphasis on technique, control, hip hinge. Typical sets/reps:
  - Main lifts: 3–4 sets of 6–8 (box squats 4x6 → 5x5 by Week 3), RDL 4x8, single‑leg RDL 3–4x8.
  - Accessories: seated leg extension (short‑arc), banded glute work, lateral band walks, calf raises, Pallof presses.
- Cardio (2x/week): low‑moderate steady + introductory intervals:
  - Cardio A: steady bike/elliptical 20–30 min, RPE 4–5.
  - Cardio B: intervals 8–10 x 30s hard / 90s easy on bike or ski‑erg.
- Recovery: daily 5–10 min micro‑routine; 2 x weekly extended mobility sessions (hip CARs, 90/90, ankle mobilizations).

Week 4 (Ramp)
- Slightly higher volume than Weeks 1–3; start adding accessory set(s) and extend cardio durations/intervals. Optional short finishers if knee tolerates.

Weeks 5–7 (Intensified block — heavy volume & conditioning)
- Strength:
  - Increase volume: add top working sets (e.g., box squats 5x5 then 5x4), add sets to trap‑bar deadlift, bump single‑leg RDL sets.
  - Preserve knee safety with belt squat/trap‑bar alternatives and partial ROM leg press.
  - Optional short conditioning finishers after one lower session — only if knee calm.
- Cardio:
  - Cardio A: Mixed‑modal HIIT longer — full pyramid + 6–9 mixed rounds (ski‑erg, battle ropes, sled).
  - Cardio B: Longer and heavier intervals — 10–12 x 20–30s power efforts / 80–100s easy then tempo 15–20 min.
  - Overall cardio volume increased; nutrition: raise carbs slightly on training days.
- Recovery: increase extended mobility to 3x/week; be proactive with icing/compression if transient swelling.

Week 8 (Consolidation & assessment)
- Reduce accessory volume ~10–15%; test a conservative 3–5RM on trap‑bar or box squat only if knee is calm (optional). Cardio slightly reduced but still moderate intensity.

Weeks 9–11 (Peak block)
- Strength priority: heavy, low‑rep top sets to enhance neural strength without high volume.
  - Main lifts: heavy triples/doubles/singles at RPE 8–9 (box squats 3–5 sets of 2–3; trap‑bar 3–4x3).
  - Accessories: lower volume, focus on single‑leg control (3–4 sets lower reps).
- Cardio:
  - Maintain quality: Cardio A shortened but intense (pyramids + 4–6 mixed rounds); Cardio B power intervals + tempo (moderate duration).
  - Reduce overall cardio volume slightly from intensified block to allow neural recovery.
- Recovery: focus on sleep, nutrition, brief mobility—reduce long mobility flows.

Week 12 (Taper & test — feel strong)
- Sharpen: big drop in volume (40–60% reduction from peak weeks), keep 1–2 heavy but short sets early in week if testing; emphasize nervous system freshness.
- Cardio: short, high‑quality bursts only (15–25 min) — no long endurance sessions.
- Testing: optional controlled trap‑bar or box squat 1–3RM early in week only if knee calm; otherwise do heavy singles/doubles for confidence.
- On‑snow: if medically cleared and client passes readiness checklist, plan a cautious re‑introduction to skiing late Week 12 (short, easy groomed runs, no moguls or deep flexion).

Nutrition (maintain weight)
- Calories: maintain at estimated maintenance; adjust ±150–300 kcal if weight drifts.
- Protein: 1.6–2.0 g/kg/day (evenly distributed, 3–5 meals).
- Carbs: moderate overall; increase peri‑workout and on high‑volume Weeks 5–7 (+100–200 kcal from carbs those days).
- Fat: 20–30% of calories.
- Supplements (optional): creatine 3–5 g/day; omega‑3 1–2 g EPA+DHA; vitamin D if deficient; whey or protein powder to meet targets.
- Hydration: 2.5–3 L/day baseline; more on long/hot training days.
- Monitoring: weigh twice weekly; adjust calories if ±0.25–0.5 kg/week trend.

Recovery & mobility (daily to weekly)
- Daily micro: morning breathing + leg swings; evening 5–10 min foam roll and gentle stretches.
- Pre‑workout (10–12 min): bike warm‑up, glute bridges, band walks, short box squats to allowed depth, single‑leg balance.
- Post‑workout (8–15 min): easy spin cooldown, targeted static stretches, foam rolling; icing 10–15 min only if irritated.
- Extended mobility: 2–3x/week (hip CARs, 90/90, thoracic rotation, ankle dorsiflexion, short‑arc knee extensions).
- Soft‑tissue: foam roller, lacrosse ball on glutes; avoid aggressive pressure over knee; use percussive devices cautiously.
- Autoregulation: daily check (sleep, knee stiffness, pain, energy). If knee swelling/pain persists >48–72 hours, drop volume and consult physio/surgeon.

Monitoring & return‑to‑ski readiness (end of Week 12)
- No sharp pain or persistent swelling.
- Able to single‑leg balance 30+ s and perform controlled eccentric step‑downs/partial squats without pain.

  - Use lacrosse ball on glute medius/hip capsule area 1–2 minutes each side (avoid direct pressure over the knee joint).
- Mobility flow (10–12 minutes)
  - Hip CARs (controlled articular rotations): 6 slow reps each side.
  - 90/90 hip rotations (internal/external rotation): 8–10 reps each side.
  - World's greatest stretch (modified, keep knee shallow): 6–8 reps each side.
  - Couch stretch (short hold) for quads – 30s each side. If discomfort at knee, use standing quad stretch instead.
  - Ankle dorsiflexion mobilization against wall: 10 reps each side.
  - Thoracic rotation (on floor or on foam roller): 8–10 reps each side.
- Activation finish (3–5 minutes)
  - Single-leg isometric hold at partial depth: 2 x 20–30s each leg.
  - Band resisted hip extension: 10–12 each side.

Phase-specific mobility progression
- Weeks 1–3 (Rehab consolidation)
  - Priorities: regain controlled range, reduce stiffness, glute and quad activation.
  - Main focus exercises: short-arc knee extension, glute bridges, single-leg RDL technique drills (bodyweight), gentle hip CARs, ankle mobility.
  - Avoid loaded deep flexion and aggressive valgus loading.
- Weeks 4–8 (Intensified block — higher volume)
  - Priorities: more hip/ankle mobility, extra soft tissue, maintain quad control in higher fatigue.
  - Increase frequency of extended sessions to 3x/week; add longer bike warm-ups (10 min) and cooldowns (8–10 min).
  - Add proactive recovery: contrast baths or compression garments after high-volume sessions if tolerated.
  - Mobility emphasis: thoracic mobility for better skiing posture and loaded carry positioning; lateral chain work for ski stability.
- Weeks 9–12 (Peak & taper)
  - Priorities: preserve mobility, reduce volume, priming for power.
  - Shorter mobility sessions with emphasis on dynamic priming and neural activation.
  - Maintain foam rolling but reduce duration; prioritize sleep, nutrition, and short activation sessions rather than long mobility flows.

Targeted mobility and rehab-style drills (progressions and cues)
1) Short-arc knee extension (controlled quad activation)
   - Position: seated with towel roll under knee; extend knee through short ROM (no pain), hold 1–2s at top, lower slowly.
   - Progression: add ankle weight or light band resistance once 3 x 12 is comfortable.

2) Heel prop / terminal knee extension (short-range)
   - Loop band around knee and anchored behind; from slight knee bend, extend to near full but only within pain-free range, hold 2s.
   - Purpose: VMO / quad control and knee tracking.

3) Controlled single-leg RDL (technique emphasis)
   - Soft bend in standing leg, hinge at hips, reach fingers toward floor; maintain neutral spine and limited knee flexion.
   - Progress from bodyweight → light DB → heavier as tolerated. Emphasize 3–4s eccentric.

4) Box squat to controlled depth
   - Use a box set to the allowed depth (~60° knee flexion). Sit back to the box and stand up with hip drive; pause lightly on the box to remove rebound.
   - Progression: increase load, reduce pause time, work on speed out of the hole.

5) Lateral lunge to shallow depth / lateral step-over
   - Step laterally to a short box or step — keep depth shallow. Focus on pushing hips back and controlling knee alignment over foot.
   - Progression: add weight (dumbbell rack hold) or increase distance slightly.

6) Hip CARs and 90/90 mobility
   - Slow controlled hip circles to improve joint integrity and excursion before loaded sessions.

7) Ankle dorsiflexion mobilizations
   - Wall ankle mobilizations with knee tracking over toes 8–10 reps; improves squat mechanics without adding knee flexion.

8) Glute med and hip external rotator activation
   - Banded monster walks, clamshells, side-lying hip raises 2–3 x 10–15 to maintain lateral chain strength for skiing.

9) Thoracic rotation + extension
   - Quadruped T-spine rotations or foam roller thoracic extensions to improve upper body posture and decoupling during skiing.

Self-massage and tools (how to use them safely)
- Foam roller: quads, hamstrings, glutes, calves. Move slowly; avoid prolonged pressure directly over the knee joint and any tender points that increase swelling.
- Lacrosse ball: glute medius and piriformis — roll for 60–90s each side; stop if pain is sharp.
- Percussive devices (Theragun): use low-to-moderate intensity on larger muscle groups; avoid direct application to the knee joint and bone.
- Mini-ball under anterior hip/IT band: short, controlled releases only; do not aggressively press into the area if it causes swelling.

In-session recovery strategies (between sets or at end of session)
- Between heavy sets: use diaphragmatic breathing and 30–60s light pedal to maintain circulation.
- Post-session: 5–10 min low-intensity spin to flush metabolites.
- Cold therapy: ice 10–15 min if knee irritated/sore; repeat up to 2x on heavier days but avoid overuse of icing if aiming for adaptation (use strategically).
- Compression: wearing compression tights or a light knee sleeve after sessions can reduce perceived soreness and swelling for some people.

Sleep, nutrition, and systemic recovery
- Sleep: 7.5–9 hours per night. If training is heavy, include a 20–30 minute nap on high-fatigue days.
- Nutrition: maintain protein 1.6–2.0 g/kg/day; increase carbs on high-volume weeks and high-intensity days. Ensure sodium and fluids to manage inflammation and recovery.
- Alcohol: keep minimal during heavy training and tapering weeks; alcohol impairs recovery and tissue repair.
- Supplements (optional): creatine 3–5 g/day, omega-3 1–2 g EPA+DHA, vitamin D if deficient — these support recovery and reduce inflammation.

Autoregulation and monitoring
- Daily check-in questions for the client (simple):
  - Sleep quality last night (1–5)?
  - Morning knee stiffness/swelling (none/mild/moderate)?
  - Pain with yesterday’s training (none/achy/sharp)?
  - Energy today (1–5)?
- Use answers to alter session intensity: if knee stiffness/swelling > mild or energy low, drop to maintenance loads, skip optional finishers, and consider pool or upper-body cardio instead of high-volume intervals.
- Objective markers: track single-leg balance time, pain-free ROM, and post-session swelling. If swelling persists >48–72 hours, stop heavy loading and seek physio.

When to contact physio/surgeon
- New sharp pain in the joint that does not settle with rest/ice.
- Persistent or recurring swelling after sessions lasting >72 hours.
- Any episodes of giving way or instability.
- Noticeable loss of function (can’t stair ascend/descend comfortably).

Sample weekly recovery & mobility schedule (example for an intensified week)
- Daily: 5-min morning breathing + leg swings; evening 5–10 min foam rolling & stretch.
- Mon (heavy lower): Pre-warm 12 min; post 10 min easy spin + quads/hamstring roll; evening short mobility.
- Tue (HIIT cardio): Pre 10 min activation; post 8–10 min cool-down spin + soft tissue.
- Wed (upper): Pre 8 min warm-up; post 5–8 min mobility; 20–30 min extended mobility session in evening.
- Thu (cardio): Pre 10 min; post 10 min cool-down; PNF stretching if needed.
- Fri (lower): Pre 12 min; post 10–12 min cooldown + ice if any irritation; evening foam roll.
- Sat: 20–40 min pool session or long mobility session (20–30 min).
- Sun: Rest; self-assess and plan next week.

Progress markers to look for
- Reduced morning knee stiffness and less post-session swelling over time.
- Increased single-leg balance time (aim 30+ s stable).
- Improved hip ROM (90/90, hip CAR ease) and ankle dorsiflexion with knee tracking.
- Greater confidence in partial squat depth and single-leg RDL control with heavier loads.
- Improved heart-rate recovery after high-intensity intervals.

Final notes
- This recovery/mobility plan is supportive, not a replacement for medical/physiotherapy guidance. Keep the physiotherapist in the loop for any persistent symptoms.

Weeks 1–3 (Phase 1 — Rehab consolidation)

Week 4 (Ramp)
- Slightly higher volume than Weeks 1–3; start adding accessory set(s) and extend cardio durations/intervals. Optional short finishers if knee tolerates.

Weeks 5–7 (Intensified block — heavy volume & conditioning)
- Strength:
  - Increase volume: add top working sets (e.g., box squats 5x5 then 5x4), add sets to trap‑bar deadlift, bump single‑leg RDL sets.
  - Preserve knee safety with belt squat/trap‑bar alternatives and partial ROM leg press.

  - Maintain quality: Cardio A shortened but intense (pyramids + 4–6 mixed rounds); Cardio B power intervals + tempo (moderate duration).
